newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India buys 570,000/T of diesel for April arrival.
newsitem.headline: India buys 570,000/T of diesel for April arrival.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has bought by tender 570,000 tonnes of 1.0 percent sulphur diesel in 15 cargoes for deliveries in April, traders said on Monday.

IOC bought five 45,000-tonne cargoes for delivery to Madras or Haldia on the Indian east coast, three 45,000 tonne cargoes for delivery to Kandla and seven 30,000-tonne cargoes to Goa or Kandla on the west coast.
This was below the 700,000 tonnes that IOC was widely expected to buy and traders said the immediate knee-jerk reaction is that the swaps gas oil market would slip.

But traders noted that IOC has issued a new tender for April amounting to 270,000 tonnes for delivery to Kandla--four cargoes of 1.0-percent sulphur diesel and two cargoes of the 0.5-percent grade. The tender closes on February 27 and is valid for a day.
European major Shell was awarded the lion's share with seven cargoes for delivery to Goa and Kandla.
Traders said all the cargoes were awarded based on Mediterranean spot quotes despite several aggressive offers based on MidEast spot quotes.
They said this could be because prices in the Mediterranean have been falling much faster at the time the tender was awarded, compared with MidEast prices.
